groups.summary: Before this change the only review terminal was an exhausted round budget: a loop could re-dispatch on an unchanged artifact, repeat the same unfixed findings for rounds, and then exit on cap exhaustion having never converged - and cap exhaustion could silently produce an unreviewed ship.
groups.title: Review loops could burn the budget without converging

groups.summary: The reviewer never decides its own budget. Every new terminal is deterministic plumbing in flowctl over persisted evidence - no new LLM calls, no new subprocess judges, no new exit codes, and the count-based cap stays enabled and untouched.
groups.title: Reviewers emit data and terminal verdicts; flowctl owns the arithmetic

Review engine: artifact-hash dispatch guard with reservation registry and write-ahead finalization journal, the three-rule stall detector over persisted findings digests, the structured-findings convergence ratchet, NEEDS_HUMAN verdict parsing plus the four verdict->status maps, system-owned SHIP reset with hash-epoch advance, and the new review-artifact / rp mode-probe CLI surfaces.

groups.summary: flowctl gains the domain-separated artifact-hash dispatch guard (refuses a re-review of an unchanged artifact with NOT_RETRYABLE, exit 1, zero mutation, --force override), the three-rule stall detector over persisted findings digests that exits 4 with ESCALATE, NEEDS_HUMAN as a first-class terminal verdict with persist-then-exit ordering across all four verdict->status maps, the structured findings.items convergence ratchet with a labeled legacy-prose fallback, and a system-owned SHIP reset that advances the hash epoch. After the first PR review pass, two follow-up commits hardened the same engine surface: in-process receipts are journaled before the round is consumed, an unusable findings history degrades instead of failing the round, and journal replay publishes the journaled criteria and findings container instead of re-deriving them from the envelope.
groups.title: Engine: unchanged-artifact guard, stall detector, NEEDS_HUMAN, system-owned SHIP reset

changeWalkthrough.thesis: Review loops get terminals that fire on measured non-convergence instead of only on an exhausted budget. flowctl refuses to re-review an unchanged artifact, escalates when two consecutive rounds show the same unfixed findings or no severity progress, and accepts NEEDS_HUMAN as a first-class terminal verdict from every backend. Alongside that, the per-surface prompts are recalibrated so severity means a named downstream outcome, low-confidence findings are suppressed before they can block, and bot prose findings on code PRs stop acting as merge gates. All arithmetic stays in flowctl - the reviewer only emits data and terminal verdicts.
